articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Tool Library
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in April.
body: The plan calls for tool library along Copper Court, with work expected to start in April. The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Brian Nowicki, who has lived in Foxglove Heights for 37 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Foxglove Heights Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Public works estimates the work will take about 37 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Letters: Kiln Court Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the April meeting. Please keep the park bench program in the budget. Many of us on Kiln Court use it every week.

Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Kiln Court for 16 years, and I want to say what a difference the Millrace Library branch has made.
Arthur Tiernan, Upper Commons

body: The group has raised $3,400 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Council Tables Crosswalk Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 33 residents spoke at Saturday’s session.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Public works estimates the work will take about 33 weeks once it starts in September.
Residents of Tannery Flats said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

Councilmember Carol Gruber asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $7,500. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Then & Now: Keystone Lane in 1996 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1996 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Keystone Lane from the corner of Fairview Road.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.

Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 1996 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Keystone Lane from the corner of Fairview Road.

articles.title: Ida Murphy, 78, Bus Driver
articles.deck: Friends remember Ida Murphy for the many years of service to Mill Hill.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Mill Hill Lions Club in his or her name.

Born in Mill Hill in the years after the war, Ida Murphy spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Mill Hill.
